     1	# Go–Zig binary flat-codec interoperability
     2	
     3	The deliverable is a shared binary-value surface on which Go v5, Go v6 and Zig
     4	can exchange upstream devalue 5.9.4 flat documents. The user corrected the
     5	previous milestone: an independently working Zig codec is insufficient when
     6	the Go peer rejects its values. Both Go modules still pin 5.9.4; this change
     7	does not claim v6 parity with upstream 6.x.
     8	
     9	## Result
    10	
    11	Extend the existing Go `*TypedArray` and `*DataView` model, without changing
    12	exported field types, to `Stringify` and `Parse`. Support all twelve upstream
    13	typed-array tags, including Float16Array, plus DataView. Transport raw backing
    14	bytes, preserve view kind/extent, repeated view identity, distinct equal views,
    15	shared backing buffers and graph cycles. Use the upstream compact/full-extent
    16	wire spelling and buffer-slot allocation order. Reducer/reviver precedence
    17	remains intact.
    18	
    19	Add `NewArrayBuffer([]byte)` as a copying constructor with distinct allocation
    20	even for an empty buffer. Existing slice literals continue to work; a nil or
    21	zero-capacity empty slice cannot express distinct buffer ownership. Decode
    22	empty buffers into owned storage and key empty buffers with positive capacity
    23	by their backing allocation. Apply the identity rule to both serializers.
    24	Document the constructor requirement for empty shared buffers. Do not change
    25	the ArrayBuffer slice type or introduce a parallel view model.
    26	
    27	Native view validation rejects unknown constructors, nil view pointers,
    28	negative/out-of-range extents and misaligned typed offsets/byte lengths. Bound
    29	arithmetic uses subtraction/division so it cannot overflow. Decoder validation
    30	checks the referenced raw slot is ArrayBuffer before hydration, then checks the
    31	revived value is an actual ArrayBuffer. Exercise self/mutual references and
    32	array-like allocation attacks with real reviver payloads.
    33	
    34	Canonical upstream-produced view documents are the common decoding contract.
    35	Go keeps upstream's constructor semantics for optional offset/count fields
    36	where its existing model can express them; Zig already documents stricter
    37	integer/arity admission for manually crafted documents. Do not silently claim
    38	their malformed-input acceptance or every JavaScript coercion is identical.
    39	Float16 adds raw storage transport and requires correct Uneval rendering in
    40	both modules: half-to-double conversion, JS formatting including negative zero,
    41	and two-byte subarray geometry. An unhandled numeric kind must return an error
    42	rather than silently emit empty elements.
    43	
    44	## Validation
    45	
    46	Port the existing complete binary fixture inputs to native Go constructions in
    47	both modules. Expectations come from the pinned JavaScript recorder, never
    48	either port. The recorded corpus covers every kind, whole/sub/empty/odd-sized
    49	buffers, aliases, cycles, floating bit patterns, BigInt storage, copied Node
    50	Buffer sources, file bytes and reducers. Independently check decoded contents
    51	and identity; a successful same-codec round trip alone is insufficient.
    52	Add targeted malformed-wire and native-geometry tests, including upstream's
    53	raw-buffer guard and reviver precedence. Keep module tests self-contained and
    54	Node-free by recording their static fixtures under each testdata/. Each
    55	module's recorder uses its own pin, regenerates its own binary corpus and
    56	records targeted Float16 and empty-shared-buffer Uneval expectations. Native
    57	tests require every fixture version to match UpstreamVersion. Update the v6
    58	change map's stale binary assumptions and malformed-view parsing work item.
    59	
    60	Add a small root `test-interop` command to normal `just test`: native Go tests
    61	emit independently constructed upstream-verified documents for each module;
    62	native Zig tests decode those documents and compare against independently
    63	constructed graphs, then emit their own documents; Go tests decode the Zig
    64	documents and check their independently constructed expected values. Exchange
    65	temporary files only. Assert nonempty complete case counts and names in all
    66	phases, and fail on missing files when the integration recipe is invoked. Add
    67	a CI job with Go and mise-pinned Zig that runs this recipe. This is a direct codec integration check, not a new proof
    68	framework or generated tracking system. Native language suites continue to run

    73	consumer copies to this runtime; go.work alone is vacuous because both
    74	consumers still import polytype's bundled codec. Report this redirection and
    75	any unavailable consumer proof explicitly. Production consumer migration

    79	native identity limitations); do not label binary interoperability as complete
    80	upstream feature parity. Retain upstream behavior coverage from the previous
    81	milestone and update stale capability descriptions.

# Plan: move polytype and skgo onto github.com/tylergannon/devalue/v5

Written 2026-09-25, when this repository was carved out of polytype at `e521921`
(v1.2.0). Until this plan is done, polytype ships its own copy of the runtime at
`github.com/tylergannon/polytype/devalue`, identical to `v5/` here at devalue
5.9.4 parity.

- **The runtime leaves polytype outright, with no alias shim.** The owner is

- **`devalue/codegen` stays in polytype**, at the same import path. It
  generates code from polytype's type grammar and imports

  import in its generated code changes.

# Adversarial review: Go–Zig binary flat-codec interoperability plan (round 02)

## Target

The revised `ephemeral/go-zig-flat-parity-plan.md` (untracked, on branch
`codex/go-zig-flat-parity` at `b55f530`), with its updated worklog
`ephemeral/worklog/20261008-go-zig-flat-parity.md`. Round 01:
`ephemeral/reviews/20261008-go-zig-plan-round-01.md`.

Caller constraints honoured: read-only apart from this artifact. The launch
prompt did not narrow the review's scope; this is a full re-review, not only a
check of the round-01 items.

## Evidence inspected

- Repository instructions: `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, `justfile`, `mise.toml`,
  `.github/workflows/{go,zig}.yml`.
- Go v5 (v6 is a copy): `uneval_value.go`, `typedarray.go`, `uneval.go`
  (`walk`, `renderTypedArray`, `renderDataView`), `stringify.go`,
  `internal.go` (`identityKey`, `formatNumber`), `parse.go` (hydrate, `Object`
  raw-slot peek at 307-322), `golden_test.go`.
- Recorders: `v5/testdata/record/record.mjs` (writes Zig fixtures),
  `v6/testdata/record/record.mjs` (does not); Zig version checks
  `zig/tests/profile.zig:98-104` and `zig/tests/binary.zig:134`.
- Upstream devalue 5.9.4 (pinned `v5/node_modules/devalue`): `stringify.js`,
  `parse.js`, `operations.js`, `uneval.js` (typed-array and DataView rendering),
  and the tests under `ephemeral/upstream-5.9.4/`.
- `ephemeral/devalue-parity/5.9.2-to-6.0.2.md`, `ephemeral/polytype-migration.md`
  (it says polytype's runtime copy is identical to `v5/`, so redirecting
  imports is feasible), and the consumer checkouts' `go.mod`/imports.
- Scratch reproductions (outside the repository) of Uneval with nil and invalid
  view geometry.

## Round-01 findings: status

| # | Round-01 finding | Plan now | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Float16 Uneval optional, and silently corrupt | Lines 39-42 require Float16 rendering in both modules and an error for unhandled kinds | Resolved |
| 2 | Uneval changes without upstream evidence | Lines 55-56: each recorder records targeted Float16 and empty-shared-buffer `uneval` expectations | Resolved |
| 3 | Interop not in CI; gated tests skip silently | Lines 65-67: case-count and name assertions, failure on missing files, a CI job with Go and mise-pinned Zig | Resolved |
| 4 | go.work consumer proof is vacuous | Lines 71-77: redirect imports in scratch consumer copies or report the proof as unavailable; polytype's bundled runtime is named as the remaining gap | Resolved |
| 5 | v6 fixtures detached from v6's pin; change map stale | Lines 54-58: module-local recording, every fixture version checked against `UpstreamVersion`, change-map update | Resolved |

## Findings

### 1. issue — Geometry validation stops at the flat serializers, so `Uneval` keeps writing wrong views without an error

**Kind:** verifiable bug / incomplete requirement (a gap created by the plan's scope).

Plan lines 11-12 scope the change to `Stringify` and `Parse`. Lines 27-29 list
the native validation: "Native view validation rejects unknown constructors,
nil view pointers, negative/out-of-range extents and misaligned typed
offsets/byte lengths". Nothing applies that validation to `Uneval`. Yet the
plan does edit Uneval's typed-array path (Float16 rendering, the unhandled-kind
error at lines 41-42, empty-buffer identity at line 23). Today
`renderTypedArray` and `renderDataView` (`v5/uneval.go:615-679`) never check
geometry. Reproduction against current v5:

```
Uneval(&TypedArray{Kind: Uint16Array, Buffer: make(ArrayBuffer,4), ByteOffset: 1, ByteLength: 2})
  → "new Uint16Array([0,0]).subarray(0,1)"           err=<nil>
Uneval(&DataView{Buffer: make(ArrayBuffer,4), ByteOffset: 3, ByteLength: 9})
  → "new DataView(new Uint8Array([0,0,0,0]).buffer,3,9)"  err=<nil>
```

The first output drops the one-byte offset: integer division in
`renderTypedArray` turns it into `.subarray(0,1)`, so the browser receives bytes
0-1 instead of 1-2. The second evaluates to a `RangeError` in the page. Neither
value can exist in JavaScript, so upstream has no output to match, and the
right result is an error. Once this plan lands, `Stringify` rejects these
exact values while `Uneval` (skgo's SSR hydration path) emits wrong
JavaScript. One model would then have two contradictory notions of what a
valid view is. Nil view pointers are already rejected by both serializers, so
the gap is geometry only.

**Required:** run the same native geometry validation in `Uneval` for
`*TypedArray` and `*DataView` in both modules. Add native-geometry Uneval tests
next to the Stringify ones.

### 2. nitpick — Malformed-wire cases should name sentinel and out-of-range buffer indices

Plan line 30 requires peeking at the raw slot before hydration. In JavaScript,
`values[value[1]][0]` with `value[1]` = `-1` or `≥ length` reads `undefined`
and throws a `TypeError`. In Go, an unchecked `p.values[idx]` panics. The
existing `Object` peek shows the guard pattern (`v5/parse.go:311-316`: `>= 0`
and `< len`). The plan's malformed-wire list (line 52) should name negative
sentinels (−1…−7) and out-of-range indices as the buffer reference, so the
guard is tested rather than assumed.

### 3. nitpick — Formatting

Plan line 67 runs well past the file's wrap width ("…runs this recipe. This is
a direct codec integration check, not a new proof"), and so does line 77.
Cosmetic only.

## Non-findings considered

- Redirecting consumer imports in scratch copies is feasible and not
  over-engineering. `ephemeral/polytype-migration.md` says polytype's runtime
  is "identical to `v5/` here at devalue 5.9.4 parity", and the plan falls back
  to reporting the proof as unavailable.
- Module-local recorders cannot clobber Zig fixtures under a different pin.
  Only v5's recorder writes `zig/testdata/*`, and the Zig tests already check
  each corpus's `devalue` version (`profile.zig:98-104`, `binary.zig:134`).
- Float16 Uneval formatting: half values are exact in float64, so `formatNumber`
  covers the elements, including `NaN`/`Infinity` (`internal.go:183-191`) and
  the explicit `-0` the plan names. This matches `stringify_typed_array_elements`
  (`uneval.js:643-648`).
- Wire spelling, slot order, the raw-slot guard and the revived-buffer check
  still match upstream (`stringify.js:315-336`, `parse.js:187-196`,
  `operations.js` `fromViewInfo`). Keying empty buffers with positive capacity
  by pointer remains sound.

## Outcome

material findings remain

args.notes:
Review written to ephemeral/reviews/20261008-go-zig-plan-round-02.md. Outcome: material findings remain.

The revised plan resolves all five round-01 findings: Float16 Uneval rendering, recorded upstream uneval expectations, interop enforced in CI with case-count checks, redirected consumer copies or an explicit unavailable-proof report, and module-local fixture recording checked against each module's pin.

One new issue: the plan's geometry validation covers only Stringify and Parse, and Uneval writes wrong views without returning an error. Reproduced on current v5:
- A Uint16Array view at byte offset 1 renders as "new Uint16Array([0,0]).subarray(0,1)". The offset is lost, so the browser gets the wrong bytes.
- A DataView at offset 3 with length 9 over a 4-byte buffer renders an expression that throws RangeError when the page evaluates it.

Neither value exists in JavaScript, so the right result is an error. After this change, Stringify would reject these values while Uneval (skgo's SSR hydration path) still emits broken JavaScript. Nil view pointers are already rejected by both, so only geometry is affected.

Two nitpicks:
- Name negative-sentinel and out-of-range buffer indices among the malformed-wire cases. In Go an unchecked raw-slot read panics where JavaScript throws, and parse.go:311-316 already shows the guard to copy.
- Plan lines 67 and 77 run past the wrap width.
